Iconic Video Vixen Gloria Velez Tells Her Life Story (Flashback)
recentItems.description:
In this flashback, we revisit Gloria Velez as she shares her tumultuous journey from Long Island to Brooklyn, opening up about her dysfunctional family life, her father’s addiction, and her mother’s struggles. At 14, Velez entered the music industry, performing at teen clubs and touring with DJ Laz and 2 Live Crew. She also detailed her experience of abuse by singer Aaron Hall, who was 16 years her senior, including physical violence and mental manipulation, as well as her fight for custody of her son.

Velez went on to transition into modeling and music, recounting her experiences working with Hype Williams, Jay Z, and other prominent artists and industry figures. She also addressed her public falling out with VladTV over creative differences and financial issues, which led to a temporary rift. The conversation concluded with Velez promoting her book, Silent Screams, which details her life experiences and time in the entertainment industry.

recentItems.title: Delta Force's Dale Comstock: I Hypnotized Myself at 15 Years Old to Be Better, and It Works (Part 1)
recentItems.description:
Become a VladStocks Member now: https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join

--------
Former Delta Force team leader and Green Beret Dale Comstock joins VladTV to trace the roots of his military mindset, from growing up in Army housing in Germany and across the United States to the culture shock of moving to San Francisco as a teenager. Comstock, author of *American Badass*, explains how at 15 he discovered self-hypnosis—what he later learned was autogenic conditioning—after a humiliating baseball experience, using repetitive thought patterns and “future pacing” to transform his performance and shape his life. He also discusses his father’s 20-year Army career, his German mother, struggling as a C and D student, joining the Army instead of college, serving in the 82nd Airborne Division, and ultimately trying out for Delta Force. The interview also highlights Comstock’s role in the Panama rescue of American Kurt Muse, a landmark modern U.S. hostage mission.

--------
Rex Holloway sits down with Vlad to detail the brutal realities of Texas prison politics, including a gang war involving the Aryan Circle and a high-ranking enemy who was blinded with industrial paint stripper inside Ferguson Unit. Holloway explains how administrative segregation worked, from cuffed escorts and shielded tiers to rec-yard “dog cages,” and describes how inmates used transfers, disciplinary write-ups, and cell placement to reach rivals despite heavy security. He also reflects on “Wizard,” a feared figure he says led from the front, and how the attack led to more time and a transfer to Estelle super seg, a lockdown facility compared to ADX and Pelican Bay. The conversation expands into how Texas prison rules differ from California and federal custody, including weapons charges, shanks, block guns, and why violence plays out differently across systems.

--------
Charleston White joins VladTV to analyze the Boosie paperwork shared by 1090 Jake and debate whether it proves snitching, “telling,” or something in between. Vlad walks through the reported traffic stop, two guns in the car, the security guard’s claim, alleged threats over a gun charge, and footage from a music video/IG Live showing Boosie with a firearm despite being a felon. Charleston argues Boosie wasn’t operating as a criminal informant but says he still “told,” opening a wider conversation about hip-hop’s paperwork culture, street codes, self-preservation, and the consequences of chasing every dollar. The discussion also touches on Trae Tha Truth, Z-Ro, Houston rap politics, No Jumper, Jordan Belfort, Atlanta, Miami, armed security, legal costs, and why “real” reputations often come with no reward. A candid breakdown of rap, law, loyalty, and image.

--------
VladTV sits down with former Mexican Mafia member Ramon “Mundo” Mendoza for a raw discussion on loyalty, violence, remorse, and redemption. Mendoza reflects on putting the gang above relationships, carrying out killings in prison and on the streets, and what went through his mind during strangulations, saying he did not take pleasure in the act and wanted victims “done” rather than suffering.  

He also details a turning point inside Kern County Jail, where 81-year-old Christian visitor Nathaniel Elrich helped him confront remorse for victims’ families. Mendoza explains how two murder cases were dismissed after a speedy trial denial motion, then describes contacting parole officer Mr. Rubio, DEA task force member Gil Avila, and the Special Services Unit to begin cooperating against active killers.  

A serious true crime interview on prison politics, faith, informants, and the Mexican Mafia.
